why: Gam (गं) is Ganesha's bija — the seed syllable that carries his essence.
Mahakaya — 'great-bodied' — praises the vast form that holds all worlds.

q: Nirvighnam Kuru Me Deva ___ Karyeshu Sarvada
why: Sarva karyeshu — 'in all works' — asks for obstacle-free effort in everything, always.
The Ganesha Gayatri: 'we know the one-tusked, we meditate on the curved-trunked.'
'May Danti — the tusked one — inspire us' closes the Ganesha Gayatri.
'Served by the hosts of bhutas and ganas' — Ganesha as the lord of all attendants.
Wood-apple (kapittha) and rose-apple (jambu) — the simple fruits he loves.
Shoka vinasha karanam — 'the cause of sorrow's destruction' — Uma's son.
'I bow to the lotus feet (pada pankajam) of Vighneshwara.'
Shashivarnam — 'moon-coloured' — the serene white radiance of the invoked deity.
'Meditate on the pleasant-faced one for the pacification of all obstacles.'
Sukhakarta Dukhaharta — 'bringer of joy, remover of sorrow' — Samarth Ramdas's aarti.
'Who showers love and grace (prem krupa) as before.'
'Morya' honours the saint Morya Gosavi of Chinchwad, inseparable from Ganesha's name in Maharashtra.
'Come again early (lavkar) next year' — the visarjan farewell.
The Ganesha Pancharatnam opens with the modak held joyfully in hand.
Rigveda 2.23.1 — 'We invoke you, Ganapati of the ganas' — the Vedic invocation.
Ganeshaya is the dative — 'to Ganesha' — hence 'salutations to Shri Ganesha'.
Ganapati Atharvashirsha: 'You alone are the creator (karta)' — then sustainer, then destroyer.

q: Ganapati ___ (the Upanishad attached to the Atharvaveda)
why: The Ganapatyatharvashirsha declares Ganesha as Brahman itself.
Vighnaharta: vighna = obstacle, harta = remover.
Ekadanta: eka = one, danta = tusk.
Lambodara: lamba = large, udara = belly.
Bhalachandra: bhala = forehead, chandra = moon.
